column1: # testdata/llm/local-endpoints.tsv — the cases of the rule "local address" (T-450).
# ONE table for every implementation of the rule. The platform (IsLocalEndpoint in
# (both through the parity stand, testdata/script-parity) and scripts/compose-lint.sh
# (rule 6 calls llm-endpoint.sh) must give the answer of the second column for the
# URL of the first. The rule is the decision of system-architect#1:
#             host.docker.internal; a one-word name (a compose service); RFC 1918;
#             link-local 169.254.0.0/16 and fe80::/10; IPv6 ULA fc00::/7;
#             the IPv4-mapped form of each of them;
#   invalid — a configuration error, not the cloud: the any-address 0.0.0.0 and ::;
#             a local host without an explicit port; a port outside 1-65535; and
#             every value normalizeURL of T-206 refuses (no http(s) scheme, user
#             information, a query or a fragment, even an empty one);
#   cloud   — everything else: public addresses, any name with a dot (.local too),
# Decisions of this table beyond the list above (T-450, recorded in tasks.md):
#   - a trailing dot is dropped for the reserved names only: localhost.,
#     api.localhost. and host.docker.internal. are local. A dotted quad with it
#     (127.0.0.1., 0.0.0.0.) is not an address to Go's netip.ParseAddr and goes
#     to DNS as a name: cloud, like 127.1. A one-word name with it (ollama.) is an
#     absolute DNS name, not a service of compose: cloud (system-architect#1 on
#   - a one-word name starts with a letter and holds [a-z0-9_-]; 2130706433,
#     0x7f000001, 134744072 and 0x08080808 are numbers, not names: cloud;
#   - a host with a character Go's url.Parse refuses (a space, \ ^ ` { | }) is
#     invalid; the characters url.Parse lets through (~ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =)
#     make a name that is not of the one-word shape: cloud. A space cannot be
#     written in this file; the parity stand holds that case (endpoints.go);
#   - a port that is written counts as explicit, :80 included; leading zeros of a
#   - "host:" with an empty port, brackets around anything but an IPv6 address, and
#     a percent sign in the host (an escape or an IPv6 zone) are invalid;
#   - only 0.0.0.0 of 0.0.0.0/8 is the any-address; 0.0.0.1 is the cloud;
#   - the IPv4-compatible ::127.0.0.1 and NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 are not mapped forms.
# Format: lines starting with # and empty lines are skipped; the first other line is
# the header; then one case per line, three fields separated by one TAB: the URL
# (printable ASCII, no spaces), the answer, and the reason in words (not compared).
# Add a case here, never to one implementation only.
